entry_conditions: Use within the observed expanded carry/place/clear support, including an open pickup approach, partial acquisition/lift, transport, lowering, an attained goal with the object still pinched, partial opening, or empty-hand retreat/transition. Causal input is two world-frame observations: qpos[0:9] (arm radians, individual finger positions in metres), qvel[9:18], tcp_pose[18:25], red_pose[25:32], blue_pose[32:39] (position metres and wxyz quaternion), and red/blue goals [41:47]. Closed fingers around 0.0183 m each with TCP/object proximity and matching short-term motion suggest coupling; approximately 0.040 m fingers suggest opening but do not alone prove release. Preserve red's observed pad status during blue handling. Actual caller target/next tags and past commands are not numerical inputs; both color identities, goals and causal motion supply the learned context. The measured open starts are support, not a hard admissibility test.
exit_conditions: Geometric achievement uses real observed object poses: rotate all eight +/-0.020 m cube corners, require each XY projection inside its own goal-centered +/-0.060 m square, and require center |z-goal_z|<=0.011 m. Red AND blue is final task completion with one satisfying observation; release, speed, hold duration and TCP clearance are not required. For a useful physical handoff, additionally distinguish still pinched, opening, and left behind: fingers near 0.040 m each, object stationary at pad while TCP separates, and continuation toward blue after red or toward the demonstrated approximately 0.300 m TCP height after blue. These physical cues guide composition rather than redefine task success.
overlap_role: This policy learns its FULL 24 expanded slices without filtering on success or transport phase. Shared bands include open red approach/acquisition (for example demo10200 80:180), red lowering through attainment, opening, released settling and the long open transition toward blue (235:430), and open blue approach/acquisition through lift (440:540). Corresponding demo10204 bands are 77:174, 230:418 and 434:532. Adjacent acquisition policies can overlap these behaviors. Goal energy is restricted to supported future attainment horizons or preservation of a goal already attained; ordinary diffusion imitation covers early pickup, lift, opening, retreat and inter-object approach, avoiding a goal predicate that would incorrectly encourage sliding resting blue.
successor_readiness: An acquisition successor should receive the actual manipulation state, not merely red_at_goal. At early overlap it must be able to finish red opening/retreat; later it receives open fingers, red remaining contained, and the current TCP trajectory relative to exposed blue. The two observations give motion direction and relative coupling, while qvel and finger aperture distinguish lowering versus retreat. For final blue handling, both pads may be attained with closed fingers (demo10204 625/632); that is valid task completion but not an empty-hand interface. A physical successor expecting an empty gripper should instead receive released-object evidence and appropriate separating TCP motion. No universal endpoint height is imposed on the red-to-blue transition.
failure_signatures: Observed corner outside a pad despite small center distance; center z outside tolerance; red leaving its pad during blue handling; object following or being dragged by TCP after intended release; fingers staying closed while a caller assumes an empty hand; or predicted progress/rollout success contradicted by real poses. Geometric attainment alone cannot reveal a failed release, and equal motion alone does not prove contact. Missing an assigned phase because of an index-based switch would be an interface failure. Stopping at first two-pad attainment is legitimate task success but may leave the intended physical handoff unfinished.
continuation_guidance: Continue this learned diffusion policy when takeover occurs during supported acquisition, placement, opening or retreat. Use current poses, finger state and direction of motion to decide invocation duration, not a preset demonstration schedule. Red attained but fingers closed or partly open calls for continued release/retreat unless the successor explicitly supports that same overlap. Red left behind and an open TCP moving toward blue is a useful transfer to acquisition, while this model itself includes the rest of its assigned red-to-blue approach. During blue, keep red achievement in context. After both goals are attained, the task may terminate immediately under its contract; optionally continue supported opening and retreat for physical composition. Outcome and progress heads do not authorize termination independently of observations. This package has no runtime action reranking or external controller.
limitations: Support comes from successful centered, nearly upright training demonstrations and descriptive boundary/overlap measurements, not policy rollout evaluation. Finger values and TCP heights quoted here are examples, not exact acceptance thresholds. Force/contact, past commands, persistent caller tags and history beyond two observations are unavailable; ambiguous dwell/intent and failed grasps/releases may not be recoverable. Containment energy is mathematically rotation-aware but no joint-action equivariance, IK, collision guarantee or unseen-edge robustness is claimed. Outcome uncertainty is not a calibrated safety margin. Training futures supervise predictions only. No release/clearance condition is added to the supplied task contract.
